title: Stream queries
description:
Books are records:

```java
// Book.java
record Book(String title, String author, int year, int pages, List<String> genres) { }
```

Answer each question in `Shelf.java` with one stream pipeline (no loops):

```java
class Shelf {
    static List<String> titlesBy(List<Book> books, String author)         // sorted by year, then title
    static Map<String, Double> averagePagesByGenre(List<Book> books)       // TreeMap: genre -> average pages
    static Map<Integer, Long> countByDecade(List<Book> books)              // TreeMap: 1960 -> 3, ...
    static List<String> genresByPopularity(List<Book> books)               // most books first, ties alphabetical
    static Optional<Book> longestBefore(List<Book> books, int year)        // most pages among books before year
    static String authorsLine(List<Book> books)                            // distinct authors, sorted, "A; B; C"
}
```

starter.Book.java:
import java.util.List;

record Book(String title, String author, int year, int pages, List<String> genres) { }

solution.Book.java:
import java.util.List;

record Book(String title, String author, int year, int pages, List<String> genres) { }

hints: `flatMap(b -> b.genres().stream().map(g -> Map.entry(g, b.pages())))` turns each book into one (genre, pages) pair per genre, ready for `groupingBy`. `Map.entry(key, value)` makes such a pair: a `Map.Entry`, the same type a map's `entrySet()` holds, read with `getKey()` and `getValue()`.

For `genresByPopularity`, count the books per genre into a map first, then stream its `entrySet()` and sort it with a comparator: `(a, b) -> Long.compare(b.getValue(), a.getValue())` puts the biggest count first, and `.thenComparing(Map.Entry::getKey)` breaks ties alphabetically.
`Collectors.groupingBy(key, TreeMap::new, downstream)` collects into a sorted map; `Collectors.counting()` and `Collectors.averagingInt(...)` are the downstream collectors you need.
